svg.title: TEB-MSU pedestrian mean radiant temperature
svg.desc: Sightlines from the chest of a sunlit pedestrian to the eaves and wall bases bound four viewing angles: sky, left wall, right wall and street floor. On the open roof the horizon through the pedestrian separates the sky and roof semicircles. MRT_ROOF marks the roof pedestrian. Adjacent pedestrians on opposite sides of the shadow edge mark MRT_ROAD_SHADE and MRT_ROAD_SUN. All receptors are 1.1 m above their surfaces. The two street cases share the same background radiation. Garden strips flank the paved road. The left strip is in the building shadow and the right strip is in full sun. One brace spans both garden strips and the paved road. Another spans the green and conventional surfaces of the roof. From each brace, two arrows carry area-averaged reflected shortwave and outgoing longwave radiation to the rooftop or sunlit street pedestrian. Parallel beams from the visible solar limb reach the pedestrians on the roof and on the sunlit road.

g.title: Local angular apertures and incident radiation in a single street cross-section
Area-averaged fluxes from both garden strips and the paved road
Area-averaged fluxes from the green and conventional roof surfaces

g.text: Surface fluxes are area-weighted. Both street cases share the width-averaged background and differ only in direct sunlight.
